# UNDERWRITING MEMORANDUM — CMRE (Costamare Inc.)

## SECTION 0 — OVERVIEW

| Item | Value | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| Ticker / Company | CMRE — Costamare Inc. (NYSE), containership owner/charterer + NML lease-financing platform | [Actual] |
| Price T0 (2026-10-02) | **$15.44** | [Actual] |
| Market cap / shares | $1.857B / 120,892,607 | [Actual] |
| Verdict | **UNDERVALUED — Accumulate (value basis)** | [Estimate] |
| Base IV (last complete desk run) | **$57.35** (MoS 73.1%; upside +271.4%) | [Estimate] |
| Bull IV | **$62.23** (+303.0%) | [Estimate] |
| Bear IV | **$37.49** (+142.8% — even the downside case is worth 2.4x price) | [Estimate] |
| Expected IV (prob-weighted) | $54.84 → +255.2% expected return | [Estimate] |
| Quarter-Kelly / capped ledger weight | 24.75% / **6.0%** (High conviction band 5–8%) | [Estimate] |

The desk's reverse DCF shows the price is reachable **only** by assuming cash flow collapses ~-59%/yr in years 3–5 — i.e., that the filed $6.1B contracted annuity evaporates in two years. No reachable discount rate (tested to 25% CoE), terminal growth, or RONIC reproduces $15.44. The market is pricing a broken business; the filings show a de-risked, contract-floored one.

## SECTION 1 — MACRO (DATA 1.5 / 1.6)

- **Rates/regime:** 10y nominal 5.24%, real 2.88%, breakeven 2.36%; curve +0.45% (steepening); IG spread 1.49%, HY OAS 3.24%. Regime vector: goldilocks 0.341 (margin 0.07, contested), reflation 0.271, tightening 0.176, stagflation 0.130, recession 0.081. Markets pricing possible further hikes (2026-09-25 theme). COE ANCHOR 9.04% used unchanged.
- **Active shock — `oil_shock` (onset 2026-09-28, up):** Strait of Hormuz closure unresolved (Iran rejected reopening; Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure; Kazakhstan cannot offset the shortage). China suspended most October refined-fuel exports; Europe reverting to coal. CPI 3.35% / PCE 3.42% — sticky inflation.
- **China slowdown:** August retail +0.4% y/y, urban FAI -7.2% Jan–Aug, record-low loan growth (2026-09-24) — a direct demand headwind for the transpacific/Asia trades CMRE's fleet serves.
- **Exposure map:** CMRE is a *charterer*, not an operator — time-charter daily rates are fixed, so bunker spikes hit charterers, not CMRE's revenue. The oil shock matters to CMRE only through (a) the elevated spot environment at 2027–28 re-fixing (Bull fuel) and (b) trade-volume destruction if Hormuz closure + tariffs (US effective rate at a historical high of 11.7%; US–Canada counter-tariffs 15–50% on $27.6B activated Sep 8) + China slowdown compound (Bear engine). Rates: with **no debt maturities until 2030** [Actual, P1 CFO] and $920M+ refinanced at lower cost, a tightening regime (p=0.176) is contained; only the pending ≤$331M Q3 close remains open [Unconfirmed].

## SECTION 2 — BUSINESS & MOAT

**Economic engines (mandate 1):**
1. **Contractual annuity (core engine):** ~**$6.1B contracted containership revenue, TEU-weighted duration 5.9 years**; **97% of fleet fixed for 2026, 94% for 2027** (TEU basis) [Actual — PRIMARY P1, as of 2026-07-24]. Fleet: 69 ships in water / ~520,000 TEU + 22 newbuilds under construction + 2 secondhand acquisitions (~152,600 TEU combined) [Actual — PRIMARY P3, 2026-10-01]. The contracted base includes post-delivery charters for the 22 vessels under construction (P1 fn. 9) — growth is pre-contracted, not speculative.
2. **NML lease-financing platform:** controlling interest; **50 assets funded/committed, >$700M invested** [Actual — P1]. FY2025: $31.2M income on ~$365M year-end book (P2, P4) ≈ 7–8% after its own finance costs — roughly at CoE, below the 9.04% anchor. Treated as a **below-COE financial annuity valued near book**; its net capital deployment is growth, not maintenance (see §3 base).
3. **Transactional/spot:** ~3–6% of fleet unfixed in 2027 [Actual, P1] — pure optionality into the post-Hormuz rate environment, not a current engine.

**Owner earnings after SBC (mandate 2):** Base **$351M** [Estimate] — derivation in §3. SBC $7.0M FY2025 [Actual, DATA 5] is already expensed in net income and is counted once via `sbc_treatment = deducted_in_cf`.

**Moat (7 factors, 0–3):** intangibles/brand **1**; switching costs **1** (duration, not exclusivity); network effects **0**; cost advantage **2** (520K TEU scale, 52 years of operating discipline, in-house Costamare Services management); efficient scale **1** (global capacity cycles); differentiation **1** (mid-size niche fit); positioning/installed base **2** ($6.1B contracted, 5.9-yr duration). **Total 8/21 → 2.5/5.** Direction: *improving near-term* (contract duration + newbuilds), *structurally narrow* — a well-run commodity business with contractual smoothing, not a durable moat.

**Financial strength:** Net debt ≈ **$1.13B at 30-Jun-2026** (debt $1,504.5M = LT $1,272.8M + current $231.7M, less cash $353.8M + T-bills $19.6M) [Actual — P4]. Liquidity $423.0M incl. restricted (P1). Interest coverage ~5x (FY2025 interest & finance costs $91.4M vs operating income $456M; P2, DATA 5). No maturities until 2030 [Actual — P1]. Dividend $0.125/qtr common (~3.2% at T0) + ~$20.8M/yr preferreds [Actual — P1/P3].

## SECTION 3 — VALUATION

**Frame & shares:** Equity frame (all pack flows are after-interest); default CoE anchor **9.04%** (Bear +100 bps credit stress = 10.04%, mandate 4); shares 120,892,607 (default; dilution factor 1.000). SBC deducted in CF. Life: **perpetual** — self-replacing fleet (vessels sold at end-of-life, $160.1M net sale proceeds FY2023; replaced via purchases/advances and the newbuild program) [Actual — 20-F cash flow statement R7].

**Base CF = $351M** [Estimate] (departure from DEFAULTS $177M, reason filed): The DEFAULTS deduct a vendor "capex" scalar of $302M as maintenance. The FY2025 20-F consolidated cash-flow statement (filed 2026-03-04) shows that $302M is exactly **"Issuance of investments in leaseback vessels" $233.1M + "Vessel acquisitions and advances/Additions to vessel cost" $69.0M** [Actual]. Only **$89.9M is true maintenance** (dry-dockings $20.9M + vessel additions $69.0M; 20 vessels dry-docked in 2026, 8 in 2027 per the 20-F). Therefore: continuing-ops OCF $536.9M [Actual] − maintenance capex $89.9M = $447.0M (NML fully internalized) vs. $336.8M (NML net deployment $110.1M = $233.1M − $123.0M collections, deducted as below-COE growth capital). I take **$351M** — conservative-leaning midpoint: NML's incremental capital earns ~CoE (zero economic profit), its existing book is valued at roughly zero rather than the ~$365M it could support. Even the desk's own reference built on the vendor base implies $31.01 = 2.0x price.

**Growth (cash flow, not revenue):**
- Base: **[-4%, +4%, +9%, +6%, +4%]** — year 1 negative reflects H1-2026 adjusted NI -18% y/y ($75.1M vs $92.5M; P1) and Q2 voyage revenue -4.8% y/y; years 3–5 step up as the 22 newbuilds deliver (first tranche of four 3,100 TEU ships Q4-2027–Q4-2028 [Estimate — imarinenews]) and their pre-contracted post-delivery rates join the annuity. Deviation from DEFAULTS levels ($155M/$158M) and above next-FY revenue growth (-0.3%) justified by the filed contracted base (P1) — `guidance_deviation_reason` passed; desk kept my path.
- Bull: **[-4%, +6%, +13%, +9%, +6%]** — 2027–28 rollover re-fixes near post-Hormuz peak levels and newbuilds charter at premium (Xeneta: FE-USWC/USEC spot +324%/+325% vs end-Feb-2026, within 18%/11% of all-time highs, 2026-09-18 [Estimate]).
- Bear: **[-10%, -6%, -3%, -2%, 0%]** at 10.04% — trade-volume shock (Hormuz + tariffs + China FAI -7.2%) and re-fixing below contract; floored by the filed contracts: Bear year-5 CF $282M ≈ ~27% of the ~$1.03B/yr contracted revenue run-rate, consistent with 94%-fixed 2027 and no charterer default assumed.

**Fade / terminal:** fade **5 years**; terminal_g **3.75%** (default; sticky inflation per CPI 3.35% supports the anchor); terminal_ronic **10.41%** (default — record median return on tangible capital 11.23%, p=0.625). **Excess cash $373.4M** (departure, reason filed: P4 balance sheet at 30-Jun-2026 shows cash $353.8M + T-bills $19.6M — H1-2026 deployment into newbuilds/acquisitions consumed ~$159M of the FY2025 year-end figure).

**Desk terminal:** Base implied terminal EV/FCF (Gordon) **19.6x**; Bear 16.5x; terminal share of value 59%. The desk returned no MRI sector band for the terminal multiple (`in_band: null`); cross-check vs DATA 8.5 P/E bands: 19.6x sits between cluster median 16.1x and industrials median 22.4x — inside the reasonable envelope, no forced reconciliation. Today's price implies ~**5.0x** FY2025 continuing-ops EPS to common (~$3.08 [Estimate: $371.7M ÷ 120.9M]) and ~5.6x consensus current-FY EPS $2.74 — an order-of-magnitude dislocation from every peer band, which is the anomaly itself.

**Reverse DCF (mandate 3b):** Neutral structure (9.04% CoE, 3.75% terminal g, 10-yr fade): solved initial growth **-33.7%** → **implied 10-year CAGR -13.8%**, band **< p50** (below the 8.9% median for the <$1B size bucket). Under my structure: implied stage-1 growth **-36.8%**; expectations gap vs demonstrated +13.8% 5y revenue CAGR = **-50.6 pts**.

**Crux (stated disagreement with the price):** input **growth_years_3_5** — my value **+6.3%/yr** vs price-implied **-58.9%/yr** (desk, this run; coe/terminal_g/terminal_ronic/fade all "not reachable", so growth is the *only* judgment input that can bridge to $15.44). A -59%/yr annuity decline means the filed $6.1B / 5.9-year contracted base is worth ~zero within two years — contradicting:
> "97% and 94% of our containership fleet is fixed for 2026 and 2027, respectively, while contracted revenues have reached approximately $6.1 billion with a TEU-weighted duration of 5.9 years." (PRIMARY P1, 2026-07-27)
> "As a result of the recent financing activity, we will have no debt maturities till 2030." (PRIMARY P1, 2026-07-27)

Size of disagreement: ~65 pts/yr over years 3–5; the price is reachable only through contract cancellation/default or a vendor-base accounting error, neither of which appears in the filings.

## SECTION 4 — SCENARIOS (last complete desk run)

| Scenario | Prob | Base CF | Growth y1–y5 | CoE | IV/share | vs T0 | Causal path |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Bear** | 0.20 | $351M | -10/-6/-3/-2/0% | 10.04% | **$37.49** | +142.8% | Hormuz closure persists into a trade war: China demand collapse (FAI -7.2%) + tariffs (effective rate 11.7%) destroy liner volumes; spot reverts to trough (Asia–Europe 12 straight weeks of declines, Loadstar 2026-10-02); 2027 rollover re-fixes below contract; off-hire days rise (Q2 print already shows them).
